outcomes: A workspace that lists extension:@putnami/cloud in agentArtifacts receives from putnami install the agency agent content @putnami/intelligence used to ship, so that extension can go without a workspace losing a skill

The Putnami routine a person already created keeps working: the skills keep their names and their paths under .agents/skills/, and every command they name is a putnami agency command @putnami/cloud runs
nonGoals: Changing what the audit, putnami-routine, rebase or routine-build skills do, beyond the commands and the settings block they name and the requirements below
Removing @putnami/intelligence or its agent content, which happens apart once @putnami/cloud ships this content
Changing this repository's own agentArtifacts or extension pins

text: @putnami/cloud declares agentContent, built from agent-src, and its content holds the skills audit, putnami-routine, rebase and routine-build, and the workers prune-apply and prune-triage.

putnami-routine keeps references/dispatch.md, references/saved-prompt.md, references/environment-setup.sh and scripts/dispatch.sh at those paths, and its dispatch allowlist stays rebase and build, build running routine-build.

No file of the content names putnami intelligence or extension:@putnami/intelligence: a command it names is putnami agency trigger, putnami agency build or putnami agency audit-attest, and a workspace that lacks a skill is told to list extension:@putnami/cloud in agentArtifacts.
The audit skill reads its settings from options["@putnami/cloud"].audit.

The rebase skill never merges a conflicted generated file by hand: it resolves and stages the replayed commit's conflicted sources, builds the file's project once with putnami build --projects <project>, stages the regenerated file, a failure only with generated-output-drift counting as its rewrite, and drops every other change the build made.
Another build failure is command_failed; a file left absent or with a conflict marker is conflict_unresolved.

requirements.text: routine-build checks out the work branch before putnami agent attach --issue <issue.number>, so the session reports to mission issue-<number> from the branch the build pushes, never from a detached HEAD or the default branch, as the last routine-build @putnami/intelligence shipped did.
